senses.gloss:
Uttaragītā
------------------------------------------
This is one of the minor Gītās composed in imitation of the well-known Bhagavadgītā. Though sometimes mentioned in the colophons of the manuscripts as forming a part of the Mahābhārata or the Bhāgavata, it is not found in the extant texts of these works. In all probability it is an independent work.
It is in the form of a dialogue between अर्जुन and कृष्ण.
As per most of the manuscripts, it has three adhyāyas (chapters) containing 122 verses in all.
Only one version contains 241 verses spread over six chapters.
There is only one commentary ascribed to गौडपाद (circa A. D. 700). It is quite useful in understanding the text.
A brief summary of the work may now be given here:
First Adhyāya (57 verses)
Arjuna asks a question about ब्रह्मन्, the knowledge of which gives immediate लिबेरतिओन्.
Kṛṣṇa replies that ब्रह्मन् which is represented by Oṁ in the scriptures is immutable and indestructible. Attaining to it, the knower is released from all bondages. Practice of प्राणायाम and meditating on ब्रह्मन् helps in this attainment.
Incidentally, Lord कृष्ण says that धर्म and अधर्म, the मिन्द्, the five senses, and the five elements accompany the जीव even after the death of one body, as long as he has not attained the highest knowledge.
Control of the senses as a necessary means of spiritual wisdom is greatly stressed.
Second Adhyāya (48 verses)
When one realises the omniscient, omnipresent ब्रह्मन्, what is the means by which one can actually know “I am ब्रह्मन्?” This is the question of अर्जुन. कृष्ण says that it is a direct experience like water becoming one with water or milk becoming one with milk.
This is followed by a detailed description of the several nāḍīs in the body (See NĀḌĪ.)
Third Adhyāya (17 verses)
This sums up the discussion and declares that the reality alone is to be sought from amongst all the different sciences. Life is too short to master the various sciences. Yogins devoted to आत्मज्ञान (Self-knowledge) do not bother to visit the various places of पिल्ग्रिमगे.
The work stresses that steady devotion to Keśava gives लिबेरतिओन् to the yogin, especially if he is free from cravings.

Utathyagītā
(‘the teaching of the sage Utathya’)
------------------------------------------
This is one of the several minor Gītās found in the Mahābhārata (vide Śāntiparva, chapters 90 and 91).
It is the teaching given by the sage Utathya (or Ucathya) to the king Māndhātā of the solar dynasty. This has been recounted by भीष्म to the king युधिष्ठिर.
The total number of verses is 96.
It delineates in detail the duties of a king, what he is expected to do and what he was to abjure.
The work repeatedly stresses that the primary duty of a king is to protect धर्म and the people under his care and not selfish enjoyment of the pleasures of life.
The following are some of his duties and responsibilities:
Sticking to the path of धर्म in his personal life and ruling the kingdom according to it; performing the वेदिच् सच्रिड़िचेस् as prescribed by the scriptures and honouring the priests generously; employing honest and efficient persons as ministers and high officers; preventing his subjects from going astray and committing sins; punishing the wicked; protecting the ब्राह्मणस् who are the custodians of धर्म; earning and spending money as per the rules of धर्म; developing enough strength to protect himself and his kingdom; protecting the weak against the strong; not burdening people by high taxation; meting out justice impartially; earning the goodwill of the people by all righteous means; destroying the enemies and strengthening the bonds with genuine friends.

Uttarakumāra
------------------------------------------
He was the son of the king विराट of Matsyadeśa. When the Kauravas invaded विराट’s capital and were taking away the royal cows, Uttara boasted that he would drive them away. Taking बृहन्नला (Arjuna disguised as a eunach) as his charioteer, he went to the battlefield. However when he saw the huge army of the enemies he was unnerved and wanted to run away. अर्जुन succeeded in filling him with courage and with him as his charioteer drove away all the Kauravas.
He participated in the कुरुक्षेत्र war for the Pāṇḍavas and was killed by शल्य, the king of Madradeśa.

Uttarakāṇḍa
------------------------------------------
This is the last book of the Rāmāyaṇa of वाल्मीकि.
See RĀMĀYAṆA for details.

Uttaramīmāṁsā
------------------------------------------
As opposed to the मीमाṁसा दर्शन of जैमिनि, which is termed the Pūrva-mīmāṁsā, the वेदान्त दर्शन of Bāda-rāyaṇa is known as the Uttara-mīmāṁsā.

uttaravedi
------------------------------------------
It means the upper or high altar. It is erected in the east, situated within the sacrificial area, but outside the yāgaśālā (shed). It is a square mound. The actual measurements differ. It is used in some सोम sacrifices.

Uttarā
------------------------------------------
She was the daughter of the king विराट, the ruler of Matsyadeśa. She was taught the arts of मुसिच् and dancing by बृहन्नला (Arjuna in the disguise of a eunuch during the ajñātavāsa, living incognito in the palace of विराट). She was later married to अभिमन्यु the son of सुभद्रा and अर्जुन.
When अभिमन्यु was killed in the कुरुक्षेत्र war she was pregnant, carrying the future king परीक्षित्. Though परीक्षित् was killed by Aśvatthāma, कृष्ण by his divine powers revived him.
